element.subject: an object on a slide (anatomy L1 object, catalogue header part or field, deck element)
element.doc: What an object is for on the slide. Block-aware rules (a field of a marked block: catalogue, our own decks) run first, then the text wording rules, then the geometry rules for text, then the rules for marks, images and shapes.

block.subject: a marked container (catalogue `containers[]`, a content/2 block) with the E2 terms of its fields
block.doc: Which content/2 block type a container is, from its item structure and the roles of its fields.

none.why: holds no field of its own: nothing to identify (the title container)

kind.subject: a whole slide (anatomy slide measurements: page, words, counts of roles ...)
kind.doc: Which slide kind a slide is (anatomy categories unified with the layout kinds).

structure.subject: a set of elements (a measured group: members, rows, columns, shared edge ...)
structure.doc: What a set of elements forms together.

primitive.subject: a drawn object
primitive.doc: What is drawn: the deck element type.

image-treatment.subject: an image as placed on the slide
image-treatment.doc: How an image sits on the slide.

mask.subject: the outline an image or shape is cut to
mask.doc: The outline geometry of a clip or a shape.

fill.subject: a paint (a background, a shape fill)
fill.doc: What a fill is painted with.

emphasis.subject: a run inside a text
emphasis.doc: How a run is set apart from the rest of its text.

angle.subject: a shape
angle.doc: Whether a shape is cut on a slant.

layer.subject: an element that overlaps text
layer.doc: Which side of the text an element is drawn on.

bleed.subject: an element at the slide edge
bleed.doc: Whether an element runs off the slide.

blend.subject: an element or gradient with a blend mode
blend.doc: Whether an element mixes with what is under it.

case.subject: a text
case.doc: Whether a text is set in a case transform.

terms.definition: A straight stroke between two points (deck `line`), or a drawn shape so thin it reads as one.

identify.why: a shape under 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick reads as a line

terms.signal: deck element type `line`; a shape under 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick

notBut.test: a shape has an area; a line has a length only (thin)

examples.positive: a 1 px hairline under a header

terms.definition: Glyphs set from a string in a face at a size.
terms.signal: deck element type `text`; a text run in a PDF / HTML

notBut.test: a word baked into a picture is an image (a logo set as pixels)

examples.negative: a logo image of a word

terms.definition: A raster or vector picture placed from a file.
terms.signal: deck element type `image`; an image XObject /

notBut.test: a shape is drawn from geometry, an image comes from a file

terms.definition: A filled or stroked geometry (rect, ellipse, polygon, path) with an area.
terms.signal: deck element type `shape`; a vector path; a colour region of a screenshot

notBut.test: a line is thin (under 0.8 % H / 0.5 % W)
an image comes from a file

terms.definition: A data chart drawn by the renderer from series (deck `chart`).

notBut.test: a group of shapes that only looks like a chart is a group until identified as E2 chart

terms.definition: A grid of cells drawn by the renderer (deck `table`).

notBut.test: a table is cells with a row / column model

examples.negative: three text boxes in a row

terms.definition: Several drawn things moved and scaled as one (deck `group`, a PDF vector group).
terms.signal: deck element type `group`; a vector group of a PDF

terms.definition: One box of a table or grid: the crossing of a row and a column. A table row (catalogue field `row`) is identified as its cells.

identify.why: a field of a block holding two or more cells: a table row
a member with both a row and a column index

terms.signal: a field holding two or more cells (td / th); a member of a grid with a row and a column index

notBut.test: an item is one repeated unit of a list block; a cell sits in a row AND a column

terms.definition: A figure set large: a number pattern (26 %, $4.1bn, 3x, 1 in 6, 659 deals) at 1.5 x the body size or more. The stat / KPI value / number of the other vocabularies.

identify.why: a number pattern (not a year / date) at >= 1.5x body in a block (a KPI value)

notBut.test: a heading is words; a big-number is a number pattern (a figure word like "Elevenfold" is a number, "No findings" is not)
a label is smaller than body; a big-number is >= 1.5x body
a lone year is a date (wording rules run first)

examples.negative: "2 key findings" at title size (a heading)

terms.definition: A short text (6 words or fewer) smaller than body that names the thing beside it: a year on a timeline, a process node label, a KPI label, a chart data label, a partner label ("Prepared for").

identify.why: a short one-field item of a block that also shows two figures or more of its own (data labels, not a 1..n numbering): a chart / diagram label
'prepared for / commissioned by' wording: names the partner mark beside it

terms.signal: words <= 6, size < body; in a block: a one-field item of a block showing >= 2 data labels of its own; partner wording

notBut.test: an eyebrow sits directly above the title on its edge; a label names the thing beside it
a caption sits under an image; a label names a data point, a node or a partner
a bullet is a line of a list that shows no figures of its own; a chart label is an item of a block that shows data labels

examples.positive: "2024" under a bar of a column chart
examples.negative: a two-line description in a card

terms.definition: One line of a list: an item of a block that holds a single text (with a marker, an indent or a rule between the lines).

identify.why: the only text of its item in a list block

terms.signal: a block field alone in its item, the block holding items

notBut.test: a description follows a heading in its item; a bullet is alone in its item
a paragraph is the whole block (no item); a bullet is one item of several
a chart label is an item of a block that shows data labels

examples.positive: "Publish rates, fees and terms" in a ticked list
examples.negative: the description under a card heading

terms.definition: The leading text of an item (its name, above or left of what it explains), or on a reference a text larger than body that is not the title.

identify.why: leads its item: the heaviest of the item's free texts (the first in reading order on equal weight)
larger than body, not the title

terms.signal: a block field that leads its item (heaviest weight, then reading order); size > body outside blocks

notBut.test: a big-number is a number pattern at >= 1.5x body
the title is the largest free text of the slide
an eyebrow is a short line above the title

examples.positive: "Answers, not links" over its description in a card

terms.definition: Running text at the body size (the size carrying the most words once the largest size is left out); in a KPI item, the text explaining the figure.

identify.why: the text of an item that holds a big-number: it explains the figure

terms.signal: size within 0.15 % H of the body size; a KPI item field after its figure

notBut.test: a description follows a heading in an item without a figure; body explains a figure (KPI) or is free running text
a paragraph is a block of its own

examples.positive: "Fintech revenue in 2025 passed half a trillion" under "$504B"

terms.definition: Body-size text under (or right of) a heading inside one item: what the heading means.

identify.why: reads after the heading of its item

terms.signal: a block field read after a field identified as heading in its item

notBut.test: body explains a figure; a description explains a heading
a paragraph has no heading sibling in its item
a bullet is alone in its item

examples.positive: the two lines under a card heading

terms.definition: Running text that is a block of its own (no item), or of 2 lines or more with no heading sibling in its item.

identify.why: the block's only run of text, outside any item (one line counts: a one-sentence statement block)
running text of 2 lines or more with no heading in its item

terms.signal: a block field without an item index; lines >= 2 with no heading in its item

notBut.test: body is a size; paragraph is a block

terms.definition: Legal wording (copyright, confidentiality, disclaimer) at body size or smaller.

identify.why: legal wording at body size or smaller (wording decides before repetition: a repeated copyright line is still legal)

notBut.test: footer text is repeated furniture without legal wording

terms.definition: The line citing where data comes from ("Source: ...", "Note: ...", "n = 1,000").

identify.why: starts with Source / Note, no larger than body (wording decides before repetition)

terms.definition: The slide number: digits only (or "page 3 / 20"), repeated as furniture or in the top / bottom band, no larger than body.

identify.why: digits only, repeated on >= 40 % of the pages at this spot
digits only, in the top / bottom band, not larger than body

terms.signal: text matching `pagenum`, furniture or in the top / bottom 10 % band

terms.definition: Text repeated at the same spot on 40 % or more of a deck's pages (the deck's furniture): brand name, deck title, running head.

identify.why: repeated on >= 40 % of the deck's pages at this spot

terms.signal: furniture (deck signature repeated on >= 40 % of pages; digits count as one sign)

examples.positive: "ACME 7" (a caps brand word + the page number) at the bottom left of every slide

terms.definition: A whole-line date (month year, Q1 2024, 7 July 2020, a lone year).

notBut.test: a year on a timeline or under a chart bar is a label (block rules run first)
a lone year is a date even when large

terms.definition: Template filler left in place ("Lorem ipsum", "Click to add", "XX", "Partner logo"). A QA finding.
Contact details or a closing line: email, web address, phone, "thank you", "get in touch" (25 words or fewer).

notBut.test: a sentence that mentions a contact centre in running text over 25 words

terms.definition: A list of names: 2 or more commas, no digits, at least 70 % of the words capitalised, 60 words or fewer.

notBut.test: a sentence with commas in lower case

terms.definition: A quotation glyph set on its own (a large “ as decoration of a quote).

notBut.test: a drawn quote shape is decor unless named

terms.definition: Who said a quote: a line of 15 words or fewer, smaller than the quote, directly under its closing line ("— Jane Doe, CEO").

identify.why: directly under the end of a quote (a text closing with a quote mark), smaller than it, 15 words or fewer

terms.signal: under a smaller text ending with a closing quote mark (gap <= 4 % H)

notBut.test: a dash bullet ("– faster growth") is not under a quote

examples.positive: "— Jane Doe, CEO" under “We moved faster”
examples.negative: "– faster growth" in a dash list

terms.definition: A short phrase directly under an image that says what it shows (2 to 30 words, smaller than body, not a figure).

identify.why: a phrase directly under a picture (within 2 % H), smaller than body, not a figure

terms.signal: text whose top is within 2 % H under an image of >= 1.5 % of the slide, overlapping it by half its width, smaller than body

notBut.test: a label names a data point / node / partner
an eyebrow sits above the title

terms.definition: A word set as decoration (a giant faded "2024", a background word): 3 words or fewer at half opacity or less.

identify.why: a word or two at half opacity or less: decoration, not copy

notBut.test: a big-number is read as a figure at full strength
a watermark is an image / mark

examples.positive: "GROW" at 400 pt, 10 % opacity, behind the title

terms.definition: The largest free text of the slide (the topmost one on a tie).

identify.why: largest free text (topmost on a tie)

terms.signal: largest size among texts no earlier rule took

notBut.test: a heading leads an item or is a smaller free text
a large figure is a big-number

examples.positive: the 56 px headline of a slide

terms.definition: A text directly under the title (gap under 1.6 x the title size), on its edge (or centred alike), smaller than the title, at body size or larger.

identify.why: directly under the title, same edge, smaller

notBut.test: an eyebrow is above the title
body is not on the title stack

examples.positive: "Key Insights Report" under a cover title
examples.negative: a source line at the bottom

terms.definition: A short line (8 words or fewer) directly above the title, on its edge (the kicker).

identify.why: short line just above the title, same edge

notBut.test: a label names the thing beside it
a caption is under an image
a subtitle is under the title

terms.definition: What no rule decides. Returned, never a guess; counted, so the vocabulary measures its own gaps. On a reference, the old anatomy role small-text (smaller than body, more than 6 words) is unknown: no test says what it is.
terms.signal: no rule of the chain holds

notBut.test: a label is 6 words or fewer

examples.positive: a 12-word line at 80 % of body size with nothing beside it

terms.definition: The brand's signature element on a slide: named by the brand (`layouts[].composition.device`, or a decor element with `frequency: always` on that slide kind) or the L4 `signature` of a reference record.

identify.why: the brand names it as its device (or the reference record names it its signature)

terms.signal: named: true (brand context) or signature: true (L4)

notBut.test: decor holds no text and is not named by the brand; a device is named
a band is a strip by geometry; a band the brand names is its device

examples.positive: a cover band element the brand's cover layout names as its `composition.device`

terms.definition: A plain fill covering 90 % of the slide or more: the slide's ground.

notBut.test: art is an image / pixel region
a panel is smaller than the slide

terms.definition: An image or pixel region covering 90 % of the slide or more.

examples.positive: a full-bleed photo behind the title

terms.definition: The brand's own mark: a mark whose file is in `brand.logos`; on a reference, a mark repeated as furniture, or a small (< 5 %) wide (aspect >= 1.2) mark in a corner zone with no partner label.

identify.why: a small mark repeated on >= 40 % of the deck's pages at this spot
its file is one of the brand's logos
small wide mark in a corner zone

terms.signal: inLogos: true; furniture mark; small wide mark in a corner (top / bottom 22 %, left / right 30 %)

notBut.test: a partner logo sits by a partner label, or its file is not a brand logo
one of 3 or more marks in a grid

examples.positive: the wordmark top left of a cover

terms.definition: Another organisation's mark: under or beside a partner label, or (with brand context) a mark whose file is not in `brand.logos`.

identify.why: small mark next to a partner label
its file is not one of the brand's logos

terms.signal: next to a partner label; inLogos: false

notBut.test: the brand logo has no partner label and its file is a brand logo

examples.positive: a client logo right of "Prepared for"
examples.negative: the brand wordmark alone in the top-left corner

terms.definition: One of 3 or more marks set in a row or grid (a logo wall, client list).

identify.why: one of >= 3 similar wide marks in a row / grid (an image, or a drawing of 3 pieces or more, holding no text)

terms.signal: a wide mark (aspect >= 1.2, 0.1 - 5 % of the slide; an image or a drawing of >= 3 pieces; holding no text) with peerMarks >= 3 (such marks of similar height sharing its row or column, itself included)

notBut.test: a chart bar is one drawn piece; a mark is an image or a drawing of 3 pieces or more

examples.positive: the fourth of eight client logos in a 4 x 2 grid
examples.negative: a lone logo in a corner

terms.definition: A data exhibit: a chart element, or a vector group of 8 pieces or more over 4 % of the slide holding 3 number labels or more.

identify.why: many vector pieces holding >= 3 number labels

terms.signal: deck chart; vectorgroup pieces >= 8, areaPct >= 4, numberLabelsInside >= 3

notBut.test: a diagram holds word labels, not number labels

examples.positive: a bar chart drawn as 24 paths with "12%" labels

terms.definition: A drawn structure of boxes, arrows and word labels: a vector group of 8 pieces or more over 4 % holding 2 texts or more (and fewer than 3 number labels).

identify.why: many vector pieces holding word labels

terms.definition: Drawn art without text: a vector group of 8 pieces or more over 4 % of the slide holding no text.

identify.why: many vector pieces, no labels inside

terms.signal: vectorgroup pieces >= 8, areaPct >= 4, no text inside

examples.positive: a line drawing of a city skyline

terms.definition: A table element: cells in rows and columns.

notBut.test: a chart draws data as marks

terms.definition: A mark or picture set faint (opacity 0.35 or less) over 5 % of the slide or more, behind the content.

identify.why: faint mark over a large area

examples.positive: the logo at 8 % opacity across the slide

terms.definition: An image of 12 % of the slide or more with transparency: a subject cut out of its background.

identify.why: image >= 12 % of the slide with transparency

examples.positive: a person cut out on the right of a cover

terms.definition: An opaque image covering 12 % of the slide or more (under 90 %).

examples.positive: the right-half photo of a cover

terms.definition: A small portrait (under 4 % of the slide), square-ish, cut to an ellipse.

identify.why: small image cut to a circle

notBut.test: a picture is not cut to a circle

terms.definition: An image of 1.5 % to 12 % of the slide.

identify.why: image, 1.5 % of the slide or more

terms.definition: A small pictogram: an image or a vector under 1.5 % of the slide.

notBut.test: a logo is a wide mark in a corner

examples.positive: a 40 px line icon over a card heading

terms.definition: A small element (under 6 %) set at a tilt (3 degrees or more): die-cut art stuck on the slide.

notBut.test: a badge is level (no tilt) and holds a short text on the edge of another element

examples.negative: a level "NEW" pill on a card corner

terms.definition: A small level shape (under 1.5 %) holding 3 words or fewer, set on the edge of another element.

identify.why: small level shape with a short text on the edge of another element

notBut.test: a chip is a pill in a row / inline, not on an edge

examples.positive: a "PRO" tag on the corner of a pricing card

terms.definition: A pill (radius >= half its height) under 1.5 % of the slide holding 3 words or fewer: a tag.

identify.why: a small pill holding a short label

notBut.test: a badge sits on the edge of another element

terms.definition: A small shape (under 3 %) holding a call to action of 4 words or fewer ("Learn more", "Get started").

identify.why: a small shape holding call-to-action wording

notBut.test: a chip labels, a button acts

terms.definition: A fill holding text with a pointer (a tail or arrow) aimed at another element.

identify.why: a text fill with a pointer

examples.positive: a speech-bubble note pointing at a chart peak

terms.definition: A row of 3 or more equal small marks or numbers in the top / bottom band showing where the slide sits in the deck (dots, bars, a track).

identify.why: one of >= 3 equal small marks in a row at the top / bottom

terms.signal: series >= 3 in the top / bottom 15 % band

notBut.test: a page number is one number

examples.positive: five dots bottom centre, the third filled

terms.definition: A row of 2 or more short texts (3 words or fewer) near the top, one of them marked active.

identify.why: one of a row of short texts with one marked active

notBut.test: labels name things, nothing is active

terms.definition: A small number, dot or icon shape at the head of an item (01, a bullet square, a step circle).

identify.why: a short text at the head of an item
a small shape at the head of an item

terms.signal: itemHead, small (areaPct < 1) or a short text

notBut.test: an icon is not tied to an item head

examples.negative: a lone dot in the background

terms.definition: A thin shape joining 2 or more markers or items of one block (a timeline axis, a step line).

identify.why: a thin line joining >= 2 items of one block

notBut.test: a divider separates groups, a connector joins items

examples.positive: the line through four timeline dots

terms.definition: A thin shape (< 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick, 2.5 % long or more) with content on both sides along its length, at least half as long as the wider side: it separates two groups.

identify.why: thin line with content on both sides along its length

notBut.test: a rule has content on one side or none (an accent under a title)

examples.positive: a vertical hairline between two text columns
examples.negative: a short accent bar under a title

terms.definition: A thin shape (< 0.8 % H or 0.5 % W thick, 2.5 % long or more) that separates nothing: an accent line, a hairline above a footer.

identify.why: thin line, 2.5 % of the slide long or more

notBut.test: a divider has content on both sides

examples.positive: a 150 px accent rule under a title

terms.definition: An outline (stroke, no fill) drawn around an image or a group of content.

examples.positive: a 2 px border around a photo

terms.definition: A filled shape with a non-axis edge (a slant; its angle is recorded).

identify.why: filled shape with a non-axis edge

examples.positive: a white wedge cut at 10 degrees across a cover

terms.definition: A strip spanning a full side (full width up to 30 % H, or full height up to 40 % W) holding no text or only furniture.

identify.why: full-width / full-height strip holding no text (furniture aside)

notBut.test: decor does not span a side

examples.positive: a 12 % H full-width colour strip at the bottom
examples.negative: a full-width strip holding the title (a panel)

terms.definition: A fill holding text, 8 % of the slide or more.

examples.positive: a purple block holding the cover title

terms.definition: A fill holding text, under 8 % of the slide.
Everything drawn that holds no text and that no other rule names (a fill, a vector shape).

identify.why: vector over 1.5 % of the slide, no other rule

terms.signal: a shape / region / line / vector no earlier rule took

notBut.test: a device is named by the brand

terms.definition: Rows of cells under a header row (content/2 `table`).

identify.why: its fields are rows of cells

notBut.test: a compare is two items of heading + description

terms.definition: Figures with their explanation (content/2 `kpis`): items holding a big-number, with a body, and a heading or not.

identify.why: half of its items or more hold a big-number

notBut.test: items lead with a heading, not a figure

terms.definition: A data exhibit drawn over its labels (content/2 `chart`).

identify.why: every field is a short label over a drawn area

notBut.test: a list shows no data labels of its own
KPIs set their figures as marked fields

terms.definition: One run of running text (content/2 `paragraph`).

identify.why: its one field is a paragraph

terms.definition: A list of single lines (content/2 `points`).

notBut.test: items have a heading + description each
chart labels belong to a block showing data labels

terms.definition: One or more quotations with attribution (content/2 `quotes`).

identify.why: half of its items or more open with a quote mark

terms.definition: People with portrait, name and role (content/2 `people`).

identify.why: half of its items or more hold an avatar

terms.definition: A wall of organisation marks (content/2 `logos`).
One to four images as the content (content/2 `image`).
Items in time order, each labelled by a date or period (content/2 `timeline`).

identify.why: its items are labelled by dates / periods (2024, Q1 2026, Feb 2025, Now)

terms.signal: labelText matches `period`, or the first heading starts with one

notBut.test: process steps are ordinals (Step 1), not dates

terms.definition: Steps in order: each labelled by an ordinal (Step 1, Phase 2, Stage 3), or joined in sequence by a connector line (content/2 `process`).

identify.why: its items are labelled by step ordinals

a connector line joins every item (one line crosses each of them) or runs through them in pieces, and the first item carries a label: a sequence. Period labels were already decided as timeline (timeline.periods), ordinals as process (process.ordinals); a sequence with any other label (01, a region) is a process. A frame rule over an unlabelled row (a comparison, a column list) is not a connector: the label is required (V1, the answer key: without it 3 lists and 3 column lists turn process)

terms.signal: labelText matches `ordinal`; or connector.crossing = items (or connector.inner > 0) with a label on the first item

notBut.test: a timeline is labelled by dates

items may be numbered 01 / 02 without being steps; a connector line joining every labelled item makes them a sequence (a numbered row under one rule drawn as a list is not separable by any visible sign: L1-35)
